narrativeReportMd:
# ImagingStudy R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. R6 keeps the ImagingStudy resource identity, but materially changes the local content model: several R4 elements are removed, renamed, or merged; key DICOM fields change JSON shape; and R6 adds ImagingStudy-specific error invariants that make previously tolerated partial or inconsistent summary data invalid.

## Scope
The analysis covers the ImagingStudy StructureDefinition in the R4 and R6 core packages plus directly related local terminology files. Base `Resource`/`DomainResource`/`Element`/datatype changes are out of scope and are not counted as ImagingStudy findings.

## Main migration themes
The largest migration theme is representation change: `modality`, `series.modality`, `series.bodySite`, and `series.instance.sopClass` all use different datatypes in R6. The second theme is model consolidation: `procedureReference` became `procedure`, `procedureCode` disappeared, and `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` merged into `reason`. The third theme is stricter conformance: R6 adds formal `ist-*` invariants for DICOM Study UID presence/uniqueness, count consistency, modality consistency, and study/series start ordering.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are the Coding-to-CodeableConcept modality change, the reason and procedure remodels, the bodySite/laterality remodel, SOP Class changing from `Coding` to primitive `oid`, and the new local invariants.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is especially important where a removed R4 field had clinical or workflow meaning with no single R6 slot: `interpreter`, `procedureCode`, `reasonReference` to `Media`, and `series.laterality`. Terminology review is also needed for the DICOM CID 29 to CID 33 modality change.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many breaks appear to align ImagingStudy more closely with DICOM semantics and newer FHIR modeling patterns, but several could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases, adding optional replacement elements, or using warning-level constraints before error-level invariants.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analyses should cover base artifacts, CodeableReference behavior, external DICOM terminology, and migration patterns involving Procedure, DiagnosticReport, BodyStructure, and HealthcareService.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 ImagingStudy has hard local breaking changes despite retaining the same canonical resource identity. Top concerns are datatype/JSON-shape changes for DICOM-coded fields, removed/renamed procedure/reason/interpreter/laterality elements, and new error invariants for DICOM UID and count/date consistency. Main uncertainty is external terminology impact for DICOM CID 29 versus CID 33 and SOP Class UID handling.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a structural transform, not just a version-label change. R4 `Coding` values often need wrapping into R6 `CodeableConcept` or `CodeableReference` structures; old element names such as `procedureReference`, `reasonCode`, and `reasonReference` must be rewritten; removed content needs a policy for extensions or related resources; and historical ImagingStudy summaries must be checked against the new `ist-*` consistency rules.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, target, datatype, and invariant changes because they come directly from the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and package indexes. Confidence is medium for terminology severity because external DICOM and SNOMED expansions were not fully compared and the ballot build may still change.

findings.title: Study and series modality changed from Coding to CodeableConcept with a broader DICOM value set and consistency invariant

oldState.summary: Both modality elements were Coding with extensible binding to DICOM CID 29.

binding.description: Type of acquired data in the instance.

semanticText.definition: R4 study modality was a list of series.modality values that are actual acquisition modalities; series.modality was the modality of the series.

oldState.narrativeMd: `ImagingStudy.modality` and `ImagingStudy.series.modality` were serialized as `Coding` objects in R4.

newState.summary: Both modality elements are CodeableConcept with extensible binding to DICOM CID 33; R6 adds ist-7 requiring study modality to equal all distinct series modalities.

binding.description: Type of acquired data in the instance.

constraints.human: If modality is present, modality SHALL equal all of the distinct values of series.modality

semanticText.definition: R6 modality includes all distinct values of series.modality and may include acquisition or non-acquisition modalities.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 changes both the datatype and the semantics of modality. The study-level list is no longer only actual acquisition modalities.

facts.note: Both remain extensible, but the referenced DICOM context group changed.
R6 formally requires study-level modality to equal the distinct series modalities.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct JSON-shape and generated-model break. An R4 `Coding` such as `{system, code}` is not a valid R6 `CodeableConcept`, which expects `coding` and/or `text`. The new `ist-7` invariant can also reject R4 data where study-level modality was a subset of acquisition modalities rather than all distinct series modalities.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Modality drives imaging routing, filtering, and display. Incorrect transforms can hide non-acquisition series such as segmentations or presentation states.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer DICOM modality information, including non-acquisition modalities, and enforce consistency between study and series summaries.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 Coding-valued modality fields as deprecated legacy fields while adding CodeableConcept modality and staged consistency checks.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goals are reasonable: `CodeableConcept` supports richer DICOM modality expression, CID 33 reflects non-acquisition modalities, and `ist-7` improves study/series consistency. A less-breaking design exists, but it would either keep two same-resource representations of modality or delay error-level consistency, which are material interoperability and validation tradeoffs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep the R4 `Coding` elements, mark them deprecated, and add a new `CodeableConcept` representation or transition through warning-level consistency rules. That would preserve most R4 instances, but receivers would need precedence rules when both old and new modality fields appear, and deprecated modality representations could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old JSON but creates duplicate modality representations and weaker or delayed consistency enforcement.

evidence.detail: R4 modality type is Coding with extensible binding to DICOM CID 29.
R6 modality type is CodeableConcept with extensible binding to DICOM CID 33 and condition ist-7.
R6 adds an error invariant requiring modality to equal all distinct series.modality values.

examples.examplesMd: Examples are fragments illustrating the datatype shape. A complete migration must also recompute study-level modality so it equals the distinct R6 `series.modality` values.

findings.narrativeMd: The modality fields are high-impact because they are common DICOM-derived elements and changed from `Coding` to `CodeableConcept`. Existing parsers, generated classes, FHIRPath expressions, SQL projections, and JSON transforms that read `modality.code` now need to read `modality.coding[].code`. The R6 definition also widens the semantics from acquisition modalities to all distinct series modalities.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid JSON using `Coding` is invalid against R6 because the element type changed. R6 content with multiple codings or `text` is not losslessly representable in R4's single `Coding` slot. Separately, a study-level modality list that omits a non-acquisition series modality can fail the new R6 `ist-7` error invariant.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap each R4 `Coding` in a R6 `CodeableConcept.coding` array. Recompute `ImagingStudy.modality` from the distinct R6 `series.modality` values, not only from acquisition modalities. Validate examples containing acquisition and non-acquisition DICOM modalities. Terminology review should confirm CID 29 to CID 33 mapping expectations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer datatype and invariant are understandable, but the old shape could have been retained for one release as a deprecated alias or mapped by a cross-version extension. The tradeoff is that dual modality fields would increase ambiguity and weaken consistency enforcement.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: External DICOM terminology was not expanded locally, so the exact CID 29 versus CID 33 code delta needs terminology confirmation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 ImagingStudy modality values were `Coding` objects, while R6 requires `CodeableConcept` at both the study and series modality paths and adds an error-level equality rule between study-level and series-level modalities. A server or validator receiving ordinary R4 JSON such as `modality: [{system, code}]` or `series.modality: {system, code}` will not accept it as R6 without reshaping every value, and historical study summaries that listed only acquisition modalities can fail the new invariant. Because modality is a core imaging routing/display discriminator and series.modality is mandatory when series are present, this looks more disruptive than the evidence shows is necessary.
keyEvidence: R4 `ImagingStudy.modality` and `ImagingStudy.series.modality` are `Coding` with extensible DICOM CID 29 binding.
R6 `ImagingStudy.modality` and `ImagingStudy.series.modality` are `CodeableConcept` with extensible DICOM CID 33 binding.
R6 root constraint `ist-7` is an error requiring study-level modality to equal all distinct series modality values.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 ImagingStudy is FMM 3/trial-use, so it is not normative, but modality is mature and central enough that a common mandatory-path wire-format break should have a clear compatibility rationale.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 Coding-shaped modality JSON is not valid R6 CodeableConcept JSON, and the R6 error invariant can reject previously valid summaries.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept the Coding shape while broadening the value set to CID 33 and introduced the summary-equality rule first as a warning or profile constraint. That would not provide CodeableConcept text/multiple-coding expressivity, but it appears to meet much of the DICOM modality goal with far less migration burden.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact assessment, but I am less persuaded that the partial alternative is too costly; the break deserves renewed design review.

findings.title: procedureReference was renamed to procedure and widened from 0..1 to 0..*

oldState.summary: R4 used `procedureReference` as an optional single Reference(Procedure).
oldState.narrativeMd: `procedureReference` linked the ImagingStudy to one performed Procedure.

newState.summary: R6 uses `procedure` as an optional repeating Reference(Procedure).
newState.narrativeMd: `procedure` can carry multiple performed Procedure references.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same target resource and nearly identical procedure-link semantics, with the R6 name shortened and cardinality widened.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `procedureReference` uses a property that is unknown in R6. In JSON, the old 0..1 value is an object, while the new 0..* value is an array. In the reverse direction, multiple R6 `procedure` references cannot fit into R4's single `procedureReference` without loss or splitting.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Procedure links support provenance and clinical context for the imaging acquisition.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a simpler element name and allow an imaging study to be associated with multiple performed procedures.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep scalar `procedureReference` as a deprecated legacy element while adding repeating `procedure` for multiple performed procedures.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple performed procedures is a reasonable R6 goal, and the shorter `procedure` name is a cleaner model. The break is partly avoidable, but preserving the old scalar field while adding the new repeating one would create two places for the same relationship and would not remove the old representation cleanly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `procedureReference` at `0..1` and introduce `procedure` as the preferred repeating field. This preserves R4 instances but leaves implementers with duplicate fields for performed procedure linkage, ambiguity when both are populated, and an indefinite deprecation burden.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids parser breaks for old instances but duplicates procedure-link semantics and requires conflict/precedence handling.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `procedureReference` as Reference(Procedure) with cardinality 0..1.
R6 defines `procedure` as Reference(Procedure) with cardinality 0..*.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments omit other required ImagingStudy content to highlight the renamed field and array-shape change.

findings.narrativeMd: `procedureReference` is not present in R6. Code that generated a scalar `procedureReference` object must write a repeating `procedure` array instead. Reverse conversion has a real data-model problem when R6 contains more than one procedure.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using `procedureReference` are invalid or at least unrecognized by strict R6 parsers. R6 instances with multiple `procedure` values are not representable in R4 without dropping values, choosing one primary procedure, or splitting the resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `procedureReference` to `procedure` and wrap the value in an array. For R6-to-R4 conversion, define a policy for multiple procedures, such as selecting a primary Procedure, creating extensions, or rejecting non-lossless conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The cardinality widening is useful but could have been introduced with a deprecated legacy alias. The chosen design favors a cleaner R6 model over direct R4 JSON compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 used a single `procedureReference` object, while R6 uses repeatable `procedure` references. Existing instances with `procedureReference` will not deserialize or validate as R6 until renamed and wrapped as an array, and an R6 instance with multiple procedures cannot round-trip into the R4 scalar without policy. The R6 goal is nevertheless coherent: one imaging study can satisfy multiple performed procedures, and retaining both old and new fields would create competing homes for the same relationship.
keyEvidence: R4 `ImagingStudy.procedureReference` is 0..1 `Reference(Procedure)`.
R6 `ImagingStudy.procedure` is 0..* `Reference(Procedure)`.
R6 definition describes the performed procedure(s) during which the imaging data was created.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises a moderate compatibility expectation, but this optional relationship changed to support a real cardinality need rather than a pure rename.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the R4 property name and scalar JSON shape are not the R6 property name or array shape; reverse conversion can lose multiple references.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained deprecated `procedureReference` while adding repeatable `procedure`, but that would duplicate procedure-link semantics and require precedence rules when both are present. Widening the old path alone would still change JSON shape from object to array.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact; I agree it is a hard migration break, but the R6 design goal and duplicate-field tradeoff make it probably acceptable.

findings.title: procedureCode was removed without a direct coded replacement in ImagingStudy

oldState.summary: R4 had repeating `procedureCode` as CodeableConcept for the performed procedure type.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could carry performed procedure codes directly on ImagingStudy.

newState.summary: R6 has no `procedureCode`; coded procedure information must be represented outside this element, typically through referenced Procedure resources or extensions.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 local ImagingStudy model only retains a `procedure` reference, not an inline performed procedure code.

facts.newValue: No direct local coded replacement; `ImagingStudy.procedure` can reference Procedure.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `procedureCode` contains an element that R6 ImagingStudy does not define. The data is clinically meaningful and cannot be converted losslessly unless a target Procedure resource or extension strategy is created.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Procedure codes are used for clinical categorization, billing workflows, analytics, and study search.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid duplicating procedure coding on ImagingStudy when Procedure can carry the performed procedure details.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `procedureCode` as deprecated while encouraging migration to referenced `Procedure.code`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing performed procedure detail into `Procedure` is a plausible goal, but the supplied evidence does not show that immediate removal of the optional inline code was necessary. A deprecated base element would have avoided loss for ImagingStudy-only feeds, though it would carry a real duplicate-data tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design is to retain `procedureCode` as optional/deprecated and specify that new R6 systems should prefer `ImagingStudy.procedure` pointing to a `Procedure` whose `code` carries the performed procedure. This preserves R4 instances but risks conflicting or stale procedure codes if both the inline field and referenced Procedure are populated.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old inline coded data but duplicates procedure semantics across ImagingStudy and Procedure.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `procedureCode` as 0..* CodeableConcept with extensible RadLex Playbook binding.
R6 has no element with id or path `ImagingStudy.procedureCode`.

examples.examplesMd: A lossless migration generally requires creating or linking a Procedure resource whose `code` carries the former `procedureCode`.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 allowed procedure coding directly in ImagingStudy. R6 removes that local field, so implementations that used ImagingStudy as a self-contained DICOM/procedure summary lose an inline code slot.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `procedureCode` is invalid in R6. The data cannot be represented in R6 ImagingStudy itself; it needs a related Procedure or an extension. R6-to-R4 is not a major issue for this specific field because R6 no longer carries it inline.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory use of `procedureCode`. If the code represents an actual performed procedure, create or link a Procedure resource and map the code to `Procedure.code`, then reference it from `ImagingStudy.procedure`. If no Procedure resource is appropriate, define a governed extension and document the loss of base interoperability.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removing the inline code is probably avoidable from a compatibility standpoint. Keeping it optional and deprecated would have preserved old instances while encouraging Procedure-based normalization.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed to distinguish procedure type, requested procedure, protocol, billing code, and DICOM procedure code semantics in real feeds.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed inline coded procedure information on ImagingStudy, but R6 has no `procedureCode` element. An ImagingStudy-only feed carrying RadLex/ordered-procedure codes loses that information unless migration creates or links a Procedure resource, which may not be present in the source exchange. Since procedure coding can drive categorization, analytics, authorization, and billing-related workflows, removing the optional inline field without a direct base replacement appears disproportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 `ImagingStudy.procedureCode` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` with extensible RadLex Playbook binding.
No R6 `ImagingStudy.procedureCode` element is present.
R6 has `ImagingStudy.procedure` as `Reference(Procedure)`, but the code itself is not carried on ImagingStudy.
freshReview.fmmEffect: At FMM 3/trial-use, the base model can still evolve, but mature optional clinical/business data should not be removed when lossless migration depends on creating another resource.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing `procedureCode` use an unknown R6 element, and preserving the value requires non-local mapping to Procedure or an extension.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have retained `procedureCode` as deprecated while encouraging `procedure` references to Procedure.code for new content. The tradeoff is duplicate procedure semantics, but the field is optional and preserving it would avoid immediate data loss.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing concern that removal is not clearly justified; I would treat this as a Revisit finding rather than merely a documented migration issue.

findings.title: reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into reason CodeableReference and Media was dropped as a target

oldState.summary: R4 had separate repeating `reasonCode` CodeableConcept and `reasonReference` Reference elements; reasonReference allowed Condition, Observation, Media, DiagnosticReport, and DocumentReference.
oldState.narrativeMd: Codes and references were separate arrays in R4.

newState.summary: R6 has one repeating `reason` element of type CodeableReference targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, and DocumentReference.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 merges coded and referenced reasons into `CodeableReference`; `Media` is no longer in the ImagingStudy target list.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element has the same reason-for-study semantics and combines the R4 coded and reference variants into the standard `CodeableReference` pattern.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 property names `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` are absent in R6, and their JSON shape does not match R6 `CodeableReference`. R4 references to `Media` have no R6 ImagingStudy target. In reverse, a R6 CodeableReference can combine concept and reference in one item, and splitting it into R4 arrays can lose the association between the code and reference.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reason for imaging can affect clinical interpretation, prior authorization, and appropriateness review.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the CodeableReference pattern for elements that can be represented by either a concept or a reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason` CodeableReference, possibly keeping Media as a deprecated target.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adopting `CodeableReference` for reason is a reasonable R6 modeling goal because it captures concept-or-reference semantics in one element. The less-breaking path would be incomplete and costly: it would keep old arrays, duplicate the reason fact, and still not represent paired concept/reference items cleanly in the R4 shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated aliases while adding `reason`, and could retain `Media` temporarily with guidance to migrate to a more appropriate target. That would preserve R4 instances but create three competing ways to express reason and maintain a target type that R6 likely intended to remove from this relationship.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old paths but delays convergence on CodeableReference and leaves duplicate or semantically weaker reason representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `reasonCode` as 0..* CodeableConcept.
R4 defines `reasonReference` with targets including Media.
R6 defines `reason` as 0..* CodeableReference targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, and DocumentReference.

examples.examplesMd: The `Media` reference illustrates an R4 target that is not allowed by the R6 ImagingStudy reason target list.

findings.narrativeMd: The reason model changed from two explicit R4 arrays to one R6 `CodeableReference` array. This breaks JSON paths, generated accessors, search/mapping code, and any implementation that used `Media` as the reason reference.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` are invalid in R6 without transformation. R4 `reasonReference` values pointing to `Media` cannot be directly represented in R6 ImagingStudy. R6 `CodeableReference` items can be split into R4 code/reference arrays, but if a single item has both concept and reference, R4 loses that pairing.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `reasonCode` to one R6 `reason.concept`; map each allowed R4 `reasonReference` to `reason.reference`. For old `Media` references, decide whether the content should become `DocumentReference`, `Observation`, another resource, or an extension. Test mixed coded and referenced reasons.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Using CodeableReference is consistent with modern FHIR patterns, but retaining the old elements as deprecated aliases would have made R4 instances forward-compatible while conversion tooling matured.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review old `Media` usage carefully; it may represent images, photographs, or other evidence with different best R6 homes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 separated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`; R6 uses one repeatable `reason` CodeableReference and drops Media from the reference targets. R4 payloads must be reshaped, Media reasons need a target-specific migration decision, and reverse conversion can lose the association when a single CodeableReference contains both a concept and reference. Even so, the CodeableReference pattern directly addresses concept-or-reference semantics, and retaining both old arrays plus the new field would create multiple competing representations of the same reason.
keyEvidence: R4 `reasonCode` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` with example procedure-reason binding.
R4 `reasonReference` targets Condition, Observation, Media, DiagnosticReport, and DocumentReference.
R6 `reason` is 0..* `CodeableReference` targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, and DocumentReference.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means the change deserves scrutiny because reasons can affect clinical context and authorization, but this is also a recognized model-consolidation pattern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the R4 element names and split arrays are absent in R6; R6-to-R4 conversion can be lossy for paired concept/reference values and Media targets.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Deprecated aliases for `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`, perhaps temporarily retaining Media, would preserve R4 instances. The cost is substantial duplication and conflict handling among code-only, reference-only, and CodeableReference forms, so the less-breaking design is not clearly better.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact finding; the break is real, but I agree with the older report's view that the less-breaking alternative has material tradeoffs.

findings.title: interpreter was removed from ImagingStudy

oldState.narrativeMd: `interpreter` identified who read the study and interpreted images or other content.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 ImagingStudy no longer directly records the interpreting clinician on the resource.

facts.newValue: No direct local ImagingStudy replacement found.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `interpreter` contains an element that R6 does not define. The element may be clinically and operationally important, but it is optional and not always populated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reader/interpreter attribution supports accountability and report reconciliation.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly move interpretation attribution to report, provenance, or procedure-related resources rather than ImagingStudy.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional `interpreter` as deprecated while pointing implementers to DiagnosticReport, Provenance, Procedure performer, or profiles for preferred attribution.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving reader/interpreter attribution out of ImagingStudy may be a reasonable normalization goal, but the computable inputs do not identify a direct R6 replacement. Because interpreter attribution can matter clinically and operationally, immediate removal is not clearly justified when a deprecated optional field could have preserved old data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain `interpreter` with deprecation text and migration guidance. This would preserve R4-valid instances while allowing R6 ecosystems to prefer DiagnosticReport, Provenance, or other workflow-specific resources. The tradeoff is a real risk of two attribution homes diverging over time.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old attribution but risks duplicate or conflicting interpreter data across related resources.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `interpreter` as 0..* Reference to Practitioner or PractitionerRole.
R6 has no `ImagingStudy.interpreter` element.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a fragment showing the removed field.

findings.narrativeMd: `interpreter` removal is a straightforward R4-to-R6 instance break and a semantic migration concern because the old field described who interpreted the images.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A strict R6 validator rejects or flags `interpreter` as an unknown element. R6 has no direct ImagingStudy field that preserves this information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Decide whether interpreter attribution belongs in a DiagnosticReport, Provenance, Procedure performer, extension, or another local profile. Validate downstream workflows that used `ImagingStudy.interpreter` for display, routing, or audit.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal appears avoidable from a wire-compatibility perspective because the old optional element could have remained deprecated while guidance pointed to the preferred R6 location.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A clinical reviewer should verify the intended R6 home for radiologist/interpreter attribution in the relevant workflow.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 ImagingStudy could identify the practitioner or practitioner role who interpreted the images; R6 removes that element from ImagingStudy without a same-resource replacement. A migration can sometimes place attribution on DiagnosticReport, Provenance, or workflow resources, but that depends on related resources and local policy. For exchanges that use ImagingStudy itself to carry reader attribution, the change is both a validation break and potential accountability data loss.
keyEvidence: R4 `ImagingStudy.interpreter` is 0..* `Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole)`.
No R6 `ImagingStudy.interpreter` element is present.
R4 definition says the element identifies who read the study and interpreted the images or other content.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use allows cleanup, but mature attribution data with clinical and operational importance needs a clear migration path.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `interpreter` contain an unknown R6 element, and moving the value elsewhere is not a mechanical same-resource transform.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated optional `interpreter` element with guidance to prefer DiagnosticReport, Provenance, or other attribution resources would preserve old data. The tradeoff is duplicate attribution homes, but that seems manageable compared with silent loss of reader attribution.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact concern and partial less-breaking alternative; I would explicitly mark it for Revisit because no direct R6 replacement was evident.

findings.title: series.bodySite changed to CodeableReference and series.laterality was removed

oldState.summary: R4 had `series.bodySite` as Coding and separate optional `series.laterality` as Coding.

binding.description: Codes describing anatomical locations. May include laterality.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented body site and laterality as two separate Coding-valued elements.

newState.summary: R6 has `series.bodySite` as CodeableReference(BodyStructure) and no `series.laterality` element.

semanticText.definition: The bodySite MAY include laterality of the body part imaged.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can code the site or reference a BodyStructure, and laterality must be folded into that representation or carried elsewhere.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `series.bodySite` JSON was a `Coding`; R6 expects `CodeableReference` with `concept` and/or `reference`. R4 `series.laterality` is not defined in R6. R6 references to BodyStructure are not representable in R4's Coding-only bodySite without resolving or flattening the referenced resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Body site and laterality are clinically important for imaging interpretation and display; losing left/right or site specificity can be unsafe.

justification.inferredGoal: Support richer anatomic modeling through BodyStructure and avoid separate laterality when it can be encoded in bodySite.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add CodeableReference/BodyStructure support while retaining deprecated flat `bodySite` Coding and `laterality` during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting `BodyStructure` and laterality-inclusive anatomy is a reasonable R6 goal, especially for complex or clinically precise imaging anatomy. A compatible transition path exists, but retaining both flat codings and richer anatomy references would create clinically significant ambiguity if the representations disagree.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep R4 `series.bodySite` and `series.laterality` as deprecated fields while adding the R6 `CodeableReference` bodySite. That preserves old data and avoids immediate left/right loss, but it forces validators and consumers to reconcile duplicated anatomy and laterality fields, and deprecated left/right representations may persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old anatomy data but keeps multiple ways to express site and laterality, with safety-relevant conflict risk.

evidence.detail: R4 `series.bodySite` type is Coding.
R4 defines separate `series.laterality` as 0..1 Coding.
R6 `series.bodySite` type is CodeableReference targeting BodyStructure; `series.laterality` is absent.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative only; production transforms should use controlled terminology or BodyStructure references to preserve laterality.

findings.narrativeMd: The anatomic model changed materially. R4 systems often stored body part and laterality as two flat codings. R6 folds this into a richer CodeableReference that may be coded or may point to BodyStructure.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `bodySite` and `laterality` JSON is invalid in R6 as-is. R6 `BodyStructure` references are not directly representable in R4. A naive transform that drops `laterality` can produce clinically ambiguous or unsafe data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 body site codings in `bodySite.concept.coding`. Preserve laterality by selecting a laterality-specific code, adding text, creating/referencing a BodyStructure, or using a governed extension. Include test cases for left, right, bilateral, and unpaired anatomy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The CodeableReference model is likely justified for richer anatomy, but removing `laterality` without a direct alias makes old data harder to migrate. A deprecated laterality field would have reduced short-term risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Clinical terminology review is needed to avoid losing laterality or creating non-standard combined body-site codes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 represented series anatomy as a `bodySite` Coding plus a separate `laterality` Coding; R6 changes `bodySite` to CodeableReference(BodyStructure) and removes `laterality`. Old R4 JSON is not valid R6 without reshaping, and a safe transform often must combine site and laterality into a single coded concept or BodyStructure. Because left/right and anatomic site are safety-significant in imaging, a migration that requires clinical mapping or can lose laterality deserves renewed attention.
keyEvidence: R4 `series.bodySite` is 0..1 `Coding` with example body-site binding.
R4 `series.laterality` is 0..1 `Coding` with example bodysite-laterality binding.
R6 `series.bodySite` is 0..1 `CodeableReference` targeting BodyStructure, and no R6 `series.laterality` element exists.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use softens the stability burden relative to normative content, but body site and laterality are clinically central enough that lossy or expert-dependent migration remains concerning.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 Coding-shaped bodySite and separate laterality are not the R6 CodeableReference shape; R6 BodyStructure references are also lossy back to R4 Coding.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have added BodyStructure/CodeableReference support while retaining deprecated `laterality` during transition. That would create conflict risk if duplicated anatomy disagreed, but it would preserve safety-relevant left/right data and permit staged migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact assessment, but I place more weight on safety-relevant laterality loss and therefore judge the design worth revisiting.

findings.title: series.instance.sopClass changed from Coding to primitive oid

oldState.summary: R4 `sopClass` was mandatory Coding with extensible binding to the DICOM SOP Class table.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented SOP Class UID as a Coding object.

newState.summary: R6 `sopClass` is mandatory primitive `oid` with no local binding.

semanticText.comment: Typically a well-known DICOM SOP Class UID but MAY be the UID of a private SOP Class.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 represents SOP Class directly as an OID string.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This mandatory element changed from an object to a primitive string. R4 JSON with `sopClass.system` and `sopClass.code` is invalid in R6; R6 primitive extensions and private OIDs cannot be converted back to a rich R4 Coding without choosing a Coding system and losing display/userSelected details.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: SOP Class identifies the DICOM object type and can influence rendering and retrieval behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent DICOM SOP Class UID as the OID value it fundamentally is, including private SOP Classes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `Coding` shape and clarify that the code carries the SOP Class UID, including private UIDs when appropriate.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing SOP Class as an OID is semantically clean, but R4 `Coding` could already carry a DICOM SOP Class UID, and extensible terminology can accommodate private classes when the value set does not apply. For a mandatory element, replacing an object with a primitive string appears more breaking than necessary to meet the substantive DICOM UID goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `series.instance.sopClass` as `Coding`, tighten its definition to require the SOP Class UID in `Coding.code`, clarify acceptable `system` conventions, and relax or document handling for private SOP classes. This would preserve most or all R4 instances while still supporting private and well-known SOP Class UIDs; the tradeoff is a less compact model and weaker type-level OID validation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances with modest loss of primitive-oid type precision and continued Coding-system convention handling.

evidence.detail: R4 type is Coding and binding is extensible to the DICOM SOP Class table.
R6 type is primitive `oid` and no binding is present.

examples.examplesMd: The transform generally extracts the DICOM UID from the old Coding code and normalizes it to an OID string.

findings.narrativeMd: `sopClass` is mandatory for each listed instance and changed from a coded object to an OID primitive. This affects validators, generated classes, serializers, and any code that expects `sopClass.code`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Coding-shaped SOP Class values are invalid in R6. R6 OID values can be mapped back to R4 only by constructing a Coding convention; any old display/system/userSelected conventions may not round-trip.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize R4 Coding values to the bare OID string expected by R6. Define how to handle `urn:oid:` prefixes, Coding.system conventions, display text, and private SOP Class UIDs. Add tests for well-known and private SOP Classes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A direct OID is semantically appropriate, but a choice or deprecated Coding form would have been less disruptive for a mandatory element.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm the exact SOP Class Coding conventions used in local R4 data before writing a bulk transform.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The mandatory SOP Class path changed from a Coding object to a primitive `oid`. R4 instances with `sopClass.system` and `sopClass.code` fail the R6 shape, and generated models change from a rich coded datatype to a string-like primitive. The semantic goal is understandable because SOP Classes are UIDs and R6 explicitly allows private SOP Class UIDs, but R4 Coding could already carry the UID value and an extensible binding did not need to exclude private classes.
keyEvidence: R4 `series.instance.sopClass` is mandatory 1..1 `Coding` with extensible DICOM SOP Class table binding.
R6 `series.instance.sopClass` is mandatory 1..1 primitive `oid` with no terminology binding.
R6 comment says the value is typically a well-known DICOM SOP Class UID but may be a private SOP Class UID.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use permits refinement, but mandatory instance-level DICOM identity is common enough that object-to-primitive conversion has a high compatibility burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: every populated R4 instance SOP Class Coding must be transformed to a primitive oid; reverse conversion loses Coding metadata such as display or userSelected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have retained Coding, clarified that `Coding.code` is the SOP Class UID, and documented private UID handling. The tradeoff is weaker primitive-level OID validation and continued system-convention handling, but it would preserve most R4 instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing avoidable-break assessment and the Yes less-breaking alternative judgment.

findings.title: basedOn no longer allows AppointmentResponse references

oldState.summary: R4 `basedOn` allowed CarePlan, ServiceRequest, Appointment, AppointmentResponse, and Task.

newState.summary: R6 `basedOn` allows CarePlan, ServiceRequest, Appointment, and Task; AppointmentResponse is removed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 ImagingStudy whose `basedOn` points to an AppointmentResponse no longer satisfies the R6 targetProfile list. The break is limited to that target type.

justification.inferredGoal: Limit basedOn to request/plan/order-like resources rather than a response resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `AppointmentResponse` as an allowed target with deprecation or guidance to prefer Appointment, ServiceRequest, CarePlan, or Task.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Limiting `basedOn` to plan/order-like resources is a reasonable cleanup goal, but the evidence does not show why the old target had to be invalidated. Simply retaining a broader target list with guidance would preserve R4 instances and still let R6 recommend better targets.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep `AppointmentResponse` in the targetProfile list, optionally mark it deprecated in narrative guidance, and tell systems to link to the corresponding Appointment, ServiceRequest, CarePlan, or Task when possible. This has a modest semantic tradeoff but avoids a hard validation break for existing scheduling workflows.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Maintains compatibility at low model cost but permits a semantically less order-like target to remain valid.

evidence.detail: R4 includes AppointmentResponse.
R6 omits AppointmentResponse.

examples.examplesMd: The reference target can often be inferred from the literal reference type when it is local.

findings.narrativeMd: `basedOn` narrowed its allowed reference target list. This is not a broad ImagingStudy break, but it is a hard validation break for data that linked studies to AppointmentResponse.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 validators can reject `Reference(AppointmentResponse)` for `basedOn`. Other R4 targets remain allowed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For AppointmentResponse references, determine whether the correct R6 link should point to the corresponding Appointment, ServiceRequest, Task, or an extension preserving the response-specific relationship.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal could have been avoided by retaining AppointmentResponse as an allowed target. If the target was semantically inappropriate, deprecation plus guidance would have reduced migration risk.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes AppointmentResponse from the `basedOn` target list. This is a real validation break for R4 instances that pointed ImagingStudy.basedOn at an AppointmentResponse, but the affected slice is narrow and AppointmentResponse is a response resource rather than an order, plan, or request. The R6 definition and target list better align the path with authorization/order traceability.
keyEvidence: R4 `basedOn` targets CarePlan, ServiceRequest, Appointment, AppointmentResponse, and Task.
R6 `basedOn` targets CarePlan, ServiceRequest, Appointment, and Task.
R6 definition describes a plan or order fulfilled by the imaging study.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means target narrowing should not be casual, but the removed target appears peripheral and semantically weaker for this path.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 references to AppointmentResponse no longer satisfy the R6 targetProfile list.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept AppointmentResponse with deprecation guidance, which would be a low-cost compatibility move. The tradeoff is that it would continue to bless a target that does not fit the refined plan/order semantics, so the narrower model seems acceptable unless evidence of real AppointmentResponse use emerges.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the current report correctly identifies a hard break and plausible alternative, but I judge the actual impact and design concern lower than a Revisit finding.

findings.title: R6 adds local error invariants for DICOM Study UID, summary counts, and start ordering

oldState.summary: R4 ImagingStudy had no local computable constraints in the StructureDefinition snapshot.

semanticText.requirements: Some R4 text described expected DICOM Study UID and count behavior, but the snapshot did not include ImagingStudy-owned invariants.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validators using only computable constraints did not enforce the R6 `ist-*` rules.

newState.summary: R6 adds eight ImagingStudy-owned error invariants; this finding covers ist-1, ist-2, ist-3, ist-4, ist-5, ist-6, and ist-8. The modality invariant ist-7 is covered with the modality datatype change.

constraints.human: series SHALL only be present if an identifier is present with a system of urn:dicom:uid
At most, a single identifier SHALL be present with a system of urn:dicom:uid
If numberOfSeries and series are both present, the numberOfSeries value SHALL match the number of series elements
constraints.expression: numberOfSeries.exists() and series.exists() implies numberOfSeries = series.count()

constraints.human: If numberOfInstances and series.instance are both present, the numberOfInstances value SHALL match the total number of series.instance elements
constraints.expression: numberOfInstances.exists() and series.exists() implies numberOfInstances = series.instance.count()

constraints.human: If numberOfInstances and series.numberOfInstances are both present, the numberOfInstances value SHALL be the sum of the series.numberOfInstance values.
constraints.expression: numberOfInstances.exists() and series.numberOfInstances.exists() implies numberOfInstances = series.numberOfInstances.aggregate($total + $this.toInteger(), 0)

constraints.human: For each series element, if numberOfInstances and instance are both present, the numberOfInstances value SHALL match the number of instance elements
constraints.expression: series.where(numberOfInstances.empty() or instance.empty() or numberOfInstances = instance.count()).count() = series.count()

constraints.human: If started and series.started are both present, the started value SHALL be less than or equal to all of the series.started values
constraints.expression: started.empty() or series.where(started.empty() or started >= %resource.started).count() = series.count()

newState.narrativeMd: R6 turns several consistency expectations into formal error-level validation rules.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are R6 error constraints. Historical R4 data that included partial series lists with larger `numberOfSeries`/`numberOfInstances`, had multiple DICOM UID identifiers, omitted a `urn:dicom:uid` identifier while listing series, or had a study start after a series start can fail R6 validation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Count and UID consistency affect retrieval, reconciliation, and display accuracy.

justification.inferredGoal: Make DICOM identity and summary consistency rules machine-checkable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce DICOM UID and count/date rules as warnings or profile-level constraints first, and avoid exact-count errors for partial summaries.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Machine-checkable DICOM identity and consistency rules are valuable, but the exact-count error constraints are disruptive because both R4 and R6 text allow known counts to be present when series or instances are empty or only partially populated. The goal is reasonable, but the evidence does not make the base error-level break clearly necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would stage these checks as warnings, best-practice constraints, or profile requirements, and would scope exact-count equality to resources that assert complete series/instance population. This preserves old partial summaries, but it cannot provide the same uniform base guarantee that identifiers, counts, modality, and dates are internally consistent.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves partial historical data but weakens base-level guarantees for DICOM identity and summary consistency.

evidence.detail: No ImagingStudy-owned local constraints are present in R4.
R6 adds eight ImagingStudy-owned error invariants.
R4 allowed count values to be larger than contained elements due to availability, security, or other factors.

examples.examplesMd: This fragment illustrates the count and missing DICOM Study UID issues. A full R6 transform must also update modality datatype shape.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a substantial set of local validation rules. The most migration-sensitive rules are exact count matching and DICOM Study UID presence/uniqueness. R4 text allowed counts to be larger than contained lists, so partial summaries are a likely break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data can become R6-invalid even when all element names and primitive types are otherwise migrated. The validation mechanism is FHIRPath error invariants on the ImagingStudy root. These are not inherited base rules.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before R6 validation, normalize identifiers so exactly one DICOM Study UID identifier with system `urn:dicom:uid` exists when series are present. Recompute counts from included series/instances or omit count fields when the resource is intentionally partial. Check that study start is not after any series start.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new constraints are data-quality oriented but could have been introduced as warnings or profile-level constraints. Error-level base constraints make the resource less tolerant of incomplete historical DICOM summaries.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The apparent tension between R6 count definitions saying counts may be present for partial data and invariants requiring equality when series/instances are present should be reviewed against the final ballot text.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds multiple ImagingStudy-owned error invariants for DICOM UID presence/uniqueness, count equality, modality consistency, and start ordering. These can reject R4-valid partial summaries, including cases where `numberOfSeries` or `numberOfInstances` intentionally report a known total larger than the populated series or instance entries. The count invariants are especially concerning because the R6 element definitions still say the counts might be present when series or instances are empty or only partially populated.
keyEvidence: R4 ImagingStudy root has no ImagingStudy-owned local `ist-*` constraints.
R6 root adds error constraints `ist-1` through `ist-8`.
R4 count definitions allowed values larger than contained elements due to availability, security, or other factors; R6 count definitions still mention empty or partially populated series/instances.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use allows adding computable quality rules, but mature historical data patterns such as partial summaries should not become base errors without very strong rationale.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with partial counts, missing DICOM UID identifiers, multiple DICOM UID identifiers, inconsistent modality summaries, or study/series start ordering can fail R6 error-level validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have introduced these as warning or best-practice constraints, or scoped equality checks to instances that assert complete population. That weakens the uniform base guarantee, but it better respects partial-summary use cases already acknowledged in the element definitions.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact concern and partial alternative assessment; the error-level count rules deserve Revisit.

findings.title: ImagingStudy.status required value set adds inactive

oldState.summary: R4 required status codes were registered, available, cancelled, entered-in-error, and unknown.

newState.summary: R6 required status codes retain the R4 codes and add inactive.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem comparison shows `inactive` added. No old status code was removed.

semanticText.definition: Inactive describes information that is no longer valid, possibly including a study removed for retention policy reasons.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using old status codes remain valid with respect to the status code list, but R6 can now send `inactive`, which an R4 required binding rejects. Since `status` is mandatory and a modifier, enum switches and business logic that assume the R4 set can behave incorrectly.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `inactive` changes lifecycle interpretation and may affect retention, display, and clinical-use decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent studies whose information is no longer valid or has been removed for retention-policy reasons.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because adding `inactive` does not invalidate R4 status values.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The new `inactive` lifecycle state has a plausible purpose and does not remove or change any R4 status code, so it is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. The main risk is runtime and R6-to-R4 handling for clients with closed R4 enums.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is an additive required-binding code, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable under the calibration rules. Using an extension or overloading an existing status would be an R6-to-R4 mitigation, not a better base R6 design for preserving R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Forward-compatible required-code expansion; older R4 clients still need enum and reverse-conversion policy updates.

evidence.detail: R4 status binding is required to `imagingstudy-status|4.0.1`.
R6 CodeSystem includes `inactive`; R4 does not.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment highlights the status code only.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because no old status code was removed. It is important for runtimes and R6-to-R4 exchange because `status` is required and modifier-marked.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A R6 ImagingStudy with `status: inactive` is not valid against the R4 required value set. R4 clients with closed enums or exhaustive status switches can fail or mis-handle the new lifecycle state.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated enums, database constraints, UI labels, lifecycle logic, and analytics to handle `inactive`. For R6-to-R4 conversion, define whether to reject, map to `unknown`, use an extension, or carry an OperationOutcome explaining loss.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Using a new required-binding code is clearer than overloading existing statuses, but a compatibility extension could have avoided R4 enum breaks at the cost of discoverability.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds the `inactive` status code but does not remove or change any R4 status code. R4 instances remain valid at this path when moving to R6. Older R4 clients or closed enums will need a policy for R6-to-R4 conversion of `inactive`, but that is a normal reverse-direction consequence of adding a lifecycle code rather than a base R4-to-R6 break.
keyEvidence: R4 required status codes are registered, available, cancelled, entered-in-error, and unknown.
R6 keeps those codes and adds `inactive`.
R6 `inactive` means the resource describes information that is no longer valid, including retention-policy removal.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use prompts a check because status is mandatory and a modifier, but the additive code does not invalidate R4 data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 `inactive` cannot be represented by the R4 required value set without mapping policy, but R4-to-R6 compatibility is preserved.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for forward compatibility. Avoiding the new code or using an extension would reduce R6 expressivity and would not better preserve R4 instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-conversion concern, but disagree that this should carry medium/high break weight for a fresh R4-to-R6 design review.

findings.title: series.performer.actor adds HealthcareService as an allowed target

oldState.summary: R4 actor targets were Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, CareTeam, Patient, Device, and RelatedPerson.

newState.summary: R6 adds HealthcareService as an allowed performer actor target.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a widening for R4-to-R6, so old instances are not invalidated. R6 instances that use HealthcareService as the performer actor cannot be represented in R4's allowed target list without mapping to an Organization, PractitionerRole, extension, or related resource.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow imaging performance attribution to a service rather than only a person, team, organization, device, patient, or related person.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding `HealthcareService` as an allowed performer actor target is a normal widening. It improves R6 expressivity and does not invalidate R4 instances at this path.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue, so no backward-compatible alternative is applicable. Mapping HealthcareService back to R4 is a reverse-conversion policy problem rather than a reason to choose a different R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Forward-compatible expressivity gain with only reverse-conversion and older-client target-union costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because target widening preserves R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 target list excludes HealthcareService.
R6 target list includes HealthcareService.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment shows the new target type only.

findings.narrativeMd: The performer actor target list widens. This is safe for R4-to-R6 but important for bidirectional systems and generated reference-target unions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 data referencing HealthcareService is invalid against R4 target profiles. R4 clients may not load or resolve that target type for this path.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and validation rules for R6. For R6-to-R4, decide whether a HealthcareService can be mapped to Organization, PractitionerRole, Device, or an extension without changing meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is a normal additive target expansion. The only compatibility issue is reverse conversion.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens the allowed performer actor targets by adding HealthcareService. This does not invalidate any R4 ImagingStudy performer actor reference. A richer R6 instance that uses HealthcareService will not fit the R4 target list without mapping or extension, but that reverse-direction issue is expected for an additive target expansion.
keyEvidence: R4 `series.performer.actor` targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, CareTeam, Patient, Device, and RelatedPerson.
R6 keeps those targets and adds HealthcareService.
The element remains mandatory only within a performer component; the target-list change itself is widening.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not create a concern where the R4-to-R6 path is strictly widening.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: HealthcareService performer actors require reverse-conversion policy, but existing R4 target choices remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking alternative is applicable because adding HealthcareService is already forward-compatible. Omitting it would only reduce R6 expressivity.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact assessment and not-applicable alternative judgment.

findings.title: series.instance.numberOfFrames was added

semanticText.definition: The number frames in a multiframe image.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additive elements do not invalidate R4 instances moving to R6. However, R6 multiframe information cannot be represented in base R4 ImagingStudy without an extension or data loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent frame counts for multiframe DICOM images.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional `numberOfFrames` is the standard backward-compatible way to add DICOM multiframe expressivity. It preserves R4 instances in the R4-to-R6 direction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue, so `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable. Extensions or loss handling are relevant only when converting richer R6 instances back to R4.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Forward-compatible additive expressivity; R6-to-R4 conversion may need an extension or accept information loss.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because the new element is optional and additive.

evidence.detail: R4 has no `ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames` element.
R6 adds `numberOfFrames` as 0..1 unsignedInt.

examples.examplesMd: R4 base ImagingStudy has no standard slot for the frame count.

findings.narrativeMd: `numberOfFrames` is additive and therefore not an R4-to-R6 break. It matters for cross-version persistence because it carries DICOM multiframe detail that R4 cannot store in the base resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid after this addition. R6 instances using `numberOfFrames` lose information if converted to R4 without an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Allow the new field in R6 models. For R6-to-R4 conversion, define a cross-version extension or document that frame count is dropped.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is a compatible additive change in the forward direction.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `series.instance.numberOfFrames`. This is a normal additive element for multiframe DICOM data and does not invalidate any R4 ImagingStudy instance. R6-to-R4 conversion may need an extension or may drop frame-count detail, but the base R4-to-R6 compatibility concern is minimal.
keyEvidence: No R4 `ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames` element exists.
R6 adds `series.instance.numberOfFrames` as 0..1 `unsignedInt`.
R6 definition describes the number of frames in a multiframe image.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not weigh against an optional additive element that preserves all R4 instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 frame counts are not representable in base R4 ImagingStudy, but R4-to-R6 validation is unaffected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is applicable. An extension would be a reverse-conversion mitigation, not a better R6 base choice.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact assessment and not-applicable alternative judgment.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 artifact is present and retains the same canonical URL, id, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag.
No min/max changes were found for same-id local elements. The material cardinality issue is the matched rename `procedureReference` 0..1 to `procedure` 0..*, which is reported separately.

Reference targets for `subject`, `encounter`, `referrer`, `endpoint`, `location`, `series.endpoint`, and `series.specimen` were unchanged. `basedOn` and `series.performer.actor` target changes are reported separately.
No local ImagingStudy modifier flag change was found for same-id local elements. Inherited modifier-extension/base modifier behavior is out of scope.
No material local `isSummary` flag changes were found for same-id elements.
No local ImagingStudy slicing changes were identified in the compared StructureDefinitions.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value changes were identified.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex value-limit changes were identified beyond datatype and invariant changes already reported.

Local binding strength generally stayed the same where elements persisted. Material binding/value-set changes for `status`, `modality`, `series.modality`, `series.instance.sopClass`, and related datatype replacements are reported. External DICOM/SNOMED expansions were not fully compared.
Serialization-changing datatype and element-name changes were found and reported. No additional local serialization representation changes were identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact maturity and standards status increased
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 StructureDefinition status is active and extensions indicate normative/FMM 6, while R4 was draft/trial-use/FMM 3. This does not change instance JSON by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Higher maturity may make implementers less tolerant of old R4 patterns that R6 formalizes with constraints.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Series performer function ValueSet adds DEV and LOC
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding remains extensible, so adding example/value-set concepts does not invalidate R4 instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 explicitly supports device and location-like performer functions in the local ValueSet, which aligns with the broader performer mapping text.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: note definition is broadened
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `note` remains 0..* Annotation and keeps the same path and type. The R6 definition describes comments by performer, subject, or participants rather than R4's DICOM Study Description-derived note guidance.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Business rules that blocked observations/findings in `note` based on R4 text should be reviewed, but the base instance shape is unchanged.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: DICOM mapping text was substantially updated
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Mapping text changes do not directly invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementations that generate ImagingStudy directly from DICOM metadata should review updated mapping text for identifier, accession, body site, performer, and endpoint handling.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited base constraints, language binding changes, extension behavior, and common element rules are intentionally excluded from this ImagingStudy report and should be assessed by their assigned base-artifact reports.

Several ImagingStudy changes adopt CodeableReference. This report assesses the local element changes, but datatype-level semantics and cross-version conversion details belong to the CodeableReference analysis.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: DICOM CID 29, DICOM CID 33, and DICOM SOP Class UID table
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The most important terminology uncertainty is the external DICOM modality and SOP Class content. Local package files reference these external tables but do not provide complete expansions.
Several removed or remodelled ImagingStudy fields likely migrate through related resources. Those target resources' own R4-to-R6 changes should be considered before defining a production transform.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not use an official rendered R4-to-R6 diff for ImagingStudy. Findings are based on direct local StructureDefinition and terminology comparison.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare against the official HL7 diff page or generated differential notes for ImagingStudy.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: DICOM CID 29, DICOM CID 33, and the DICOM SOP Class table were referenced by URL but not expanded locally. Terminology impact for modality and SOP Class is therefore based on binding URL and datatype changes, not complete code-level comparison.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Obtain authoritative DICOM context group and SOP Class expansions for the relevant publication dates.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The body-site binding is example strength and the local R6 ValueSet representation differs from R4, but a complete SNOMED CT expansion comparison was not performed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use a terminology server with the relevant SNOMED CT edition to compare body-site coverage and laterality modeling.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build marked not for publication in package metadata. Details may change before a final R6 release.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final published R6 core package.
